div.l: Now be my fadir soule that is dede
But ye be mery I wil geue you myn̄ hede
Hold up your handes withouten more speche
Oure counseil was not long forto seche
Vs thought it was not wurth to make it nyce
And grauntid him withouten more avise
And bad him sey his verdit as him lest
¶ Lordinges coth he now herkneth for the best
But take it not in disdeyne I you prayen̄
This is the point to speken short ⁊and playn̄
That eche of you to short wᵗith oure weye
In this viage shalle telle tales twey
To Cauntirbury ward I mene it so
And homward ye shullen telle othir two .
Of auentures that whilom haue befalle
And which of you that berith him best of alle
That is to sey that tellith in this case .
Tales of best sentence ⁊and most solace
Shal haue a Souper at oure aldir cost
Here in this place sitting by this post
When̄ that we come ageyn fro Caunt̉erbury
And forto make you the more mery
I wil myselue goodly with you ride
Right at myn̄ ovne cost ⁊and be your͗e gide
And whoso wil my Iugement withsey
Shal pay alle that we spend by the wey
And if ye vouchsave that it be so
Telle me anone without wurdis mo
And I wil erly shape me therfore
This thingis were grauntid ⁊and our͗e othis swore
With ful glad hert / and preyd him also
That he wold vouchsave forto do so
And that he wold ben̄ oure goủernour͗e
And of oure tales Iuge and reportour͗e
And sette a Souper at a certeyn̄ price
And we wil rulid be at his diuise
In high and low / ⁊and thus by one assent
We ben̄ accordid to stond to his Iugement
And therupon̄ the wine was fette anone
We dranken and to rest wenten echone
